name: Xenia Hotels & Resorts
reason: Upper-upscale hotel REIT with FFO/share of 1.76 still below 2015's 2.15, 2020 loss of -0.82 in the downturn, and net debt/EBITDA 5.1x: a cyclical lodging business with no special edge.

name: XPEL
reason: High returns (ROIC ~29%, net cash) and 23% 5y EPS CAGR, but paint-protection film is a discretionary auto-aftermarket product facing cheaper Chinese film, OEM/dealer channel shifts and single-source film supply; EPS fell 14% in 2024, so a 10-year forecast is not confident.

name: Expro
reason: Oilfield services set by upstream energy capex: ten years of mostly losses (10y avg EBIT margin -6.6%, ROIC -8.8%) and shares up 12.8%/yr through the Frank's merger.

name: Xylem
reason: Leading water-technology franchise (pumps, treatment, smart metering) on secular water-infrastructure and scarcity drivers; 10y EPS CAGR 10.6% with growth of at least 7% in 8 of 10 years, net debt/EBITDA 0.5x, and consensus about 10%/yr. Watch: margin is at a 10y high (14.6%) and Evoqua (acq/FCF 0.55, shares +3%/yr) flatters growth.

name: Block
reason: Fintech built on Cash App consumer lending/BNPL credit, bitcoin revenue and fierce payments competition; 10y average ROIC -0.6%, a 2,906% adjusted-vs-GAAP gap from SBC, and shares up 6.4%/yr make the earnings path impossible to forecast with confidence.

name: Clear Secure
reason: Only about 3 years of profits, and revenue is concentrated in airport lanes that depend on TSA and airport concessions; TSA's own touchless-ID/PreCheck rollout and regulatory scrutiny are a credible threat within 5 years.

name: Zebra Technologies
reason: Strong share in barcode/mobile-computing hardware, but enterprise capex is cyclical (EPS -44% in 2023), 5y EPS CAGR is only 4.4%, growth is acquisition-heavy (acq/FCF 0.59; Elo, Photoneo) and net debt/EBITDA is 2.5x.

name: Zoom Communications
reason: Video meetings have matured into a commodity alongside Microsoft Teams and Google Meet, and AI is an added threat; consensus EPS growth is only 3-5% and the ~283% adjusted-vs-GAAP gap from SBC means there is no route to 7%+ despite net cash.
